:::{.proof}
Let $x^*$ be a local minimizer of $f$,
so there is a $\tolin > 0$ with $f(x^*) \le f(x)$
whenever $\norm{x - x^*} < \tolin$ (@def-local-minimizer).
Suppose $x^*$ is not a global minimizer (@def-global-minimizer).
Then some $y \in \reals^p$ has $f(y) < f(x^*)$,
and in particular $y \ne x^*$.

Let $t = \min\left\{\tfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{\tolin}{2 \norm{y - x^*}}\right\}$,
so $t \in (0, 1)$,
and let $z = t y + (1 - t) x^*$.
Then $z - x^* = t (y - x^*)$,
so $\norm{z - x^*} = t \norm{y - x^*} \le \tolin / 2 < \tolin$.

By convexity,
$$
f(z) \le t f(y) + (1 - t) f(x^*) < t f(x^*) + (1 - t) f(x^*) = f(x^*),
$$
where the strict inequality uses $t > 0$ and $f(y) < f(x^*)$.
So $f(z) < f(x^*)$ with $\norm{z - x^*} < \tolin$,
which contradicts $x^*$ being a local minimizer.
Hence $x^*$ is a global minimizer.
:::
